lessons.what: Shows which programs have which files (or ports) open.
lessons.when: 'Device is busy' when ejecting a pendrive. Who's still using it?
lessons.tip: In Linux, almost everything is a file. Even network ports.

lessons.what: Shows every request a program makes to the system.
lessons.when: A program fails silently. Spy on what it's actually trying to do.
lessons.tip: Look for '= -1 ENOENT': a file it couldn't find.

lessons.what: Lists the libraries a program needs to run.
lessons.when: 'error while loading shared libraries'. Which one is missing?
lessons.tip: 'not found' in the output = your missing library.

lessons.man: arbitrary TCP and UDP connections and listens
lessons.what: Opens raw network connections: the 'Swiss army knife' of networking.
lessons.when: Checking if a port on a server is open, or a 2-terminal chat demo.
lessons.tip: -z just scans, -v explains, -l listens.

lessons.man: print the route packets trace to network host
lessons.what: Shows every stop your data takes to reach a website.
lessons.when: Internet is slow. Is the problem your router or far away?
lessons.tip: Hop 1 is usually your own Wi-Fi router.

quiz.why: A required shared library isn't installed.
Each network hop on the way.

lessons.what: Copies data byte by byte. Often used to make bootable USBs.
lessons.when: Writing a Linux ISO to a pendrive to install Linux on another PC.
example: $ sudo dd if=ubuntu.iso of=/dev/sdb bs=4M status=progress
lessons.tip: Nicknamed 'disk destroyer'. Triple-check of=!

lessons.what: Shows each partition's UUID, label and filesystem type.
lessons.when: Is this pendrive FAT32 or ext4? Will Windows read it?
lessons.tip: vfat = FAT32, works on almost every device.

lessons.what: Views and edits disk partitions.
lessons.when: Checking how a disk is divided before installing a second OS.
lessons.tip: -l only lists. Nothing changes until you press w.

lessons.what: Formats a partition with a filesystem (erases everything on it).
lessons.when: Formatting a pendrive fresh, like 'Format' in Windows.
lessons.tip: ERASES the partition. Double-check with lsblk first.

lessons.what: Safely detaches a drive before you unplug it.
lessons.when: Before pulling out your pendrive. Always.
lessons.tip: It's umount, not unmount. Yes, really.

quiz.q: mkfs does what to the partition?
How is the unmount command spelled?

lessons.what: Installs, updates and removes software on Ubuntu/Debian.
lessons.when: Installing VLC, Git or Python with one command. No setup wizards.
lessons.tip: update refreshes the list, upgrade installs updates.

lessons.what: Low-level tool for .deb packages, the engine under apt.
lessons.when: You downloaded a .deb file (like VS Code or Chrome).
lessons.tip: Dependency errors? Run sudo apt -f install.

lessons.man: program for managing a netfilter firewall
lessons.what: Easy firewall: choose what network traffic is allowed in.
lessons.when: Turning on basic protection on your laptop in 2 commands.
lessons.tip: On a remote server, allow ssh BEFORE enabling!

lessons.man: show a listing of last logged in users
lessons.what: Shows the history of logins and reboots.
lessons.when: Did someone log into your account while you were away?
example: user   tty2   Tue Nov 10 09:01  still logged in
lessons.tip: last reboot shows when the PC restarted.

lessons.man: Show who is logged on and what they are doing.
lessons.what: Shows who's logged in AND what they are running right now.
lessons.when: Lab server is slow. Who's on it and what are they running?
lessons.tip: The shortest command in Linux? Contender for sure.

quiz.q: To install a downloaded .deb file you use...
Before ufw enable on a remote server you must...

quiz.why: Reboot entries from the login history.

lessons.man: check file types and compare values
lessons.what: Checks a condition: does a file exist? Is a number bigger?
lessons.when: In scripts: 'only back up if the folder exists'.
lessons.tip: [ ... ] is the same as test. Spaces matter!

lessons.man: Read a line from the standard input and split it into fields.
lessons.what: Asks the user to type something and stores it in a variable.
lessons.when: Making your script interactive: 'Enter your name:'.
lessons.tip: -s hides input (for passwords).

lessons.what: Does simple maths and string operations.
lessons.when: Quick calculations inside older shell scripts.
lessons.tip: Modern bash: $(( )) is easier.

lessons.what: Shuffles lines randomly, or picks random items.
lessons.when: Picking a random student for the presentation. Fair and square.
lessons.tip: -n picks how many, -i gives a number range.

lessons.man: output a string repeatedly until killed
lessons.what: Prints 'y' (or any text) forever.
lessons.when: Auto-answering 'yes' to every question a command asks.
lessons.tip: Most installers have -y, but yes works for anything.

quiz.why: -f = exists and is a regular file.

quiz.q: What does yes print by default?

lessons.what: The shell you've been typing into all month. It can also run script files.
lessons.when: Turning 10 commands you always type into one file you run.
lessons.tip: #!/bin/bash on line 1 tells Linux who runs the file.

lessons.man: Set or unset values of shell options and positional parameters.
lessons.what: Turns on safety settings for your scripts.
lessons.when: Stop a script the moment something fails, instead of causing chaos.
lessons.tip: -e stop on error, -u no unset variables, -x debug.

lessons.what: Runs cleanup code when a script exits or gets interrupted.
lessons.when: Delete temporary files even if someone hits Ctrl + C.
lessons.tip: EXIT runs on every exit, good or bad.

lessons.what: Ends a script or shell with a status code.
lessons.when: Telling the world 'this failed' (non-zero) or 'all good' (0).
lessons.tip: $? holds the last exit code. 0 = success.

lessons.man: Wait for job completion and return exit status.
lessons.what: Pauses a script until background jobs finish.
lessons.when: Run 3 downloads in parallel, then continue only when all are done.
lessons.tip: & runs in background, wait gathers them back.

quiz.q: What does #!/bin/bash at the top do?
options: Tells Linux to run it with bash
